title: An efficient algorithm for entropic optimal transport under martingale-type constraints

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to solve martingale optimal transport (MOT) problems with supermartingale constraints, which are challenging due to the presence of \(O(n)\) equality/inequality constraints at each source point. Paper [10] explores the structure of solutions to nonlinear martingale optimal transport problems, and paper [12] establishes numerical methods for solving MOT problems, including discretization and relaxation of martingale constraints. Both papers address the same problem-class level objective of solving MOT problems with constraints, making the purpose covered.

### Mechanism
The contribution introduces an entropic regularization formulation for MOT problems with approximate constraint satisfaction, along with a Sinkhorn-type algorithm and a sparse Newton iteration method (SNS) leveraging the Hessian's sparsity, warm initialization, and geometric \(\eta\)-scheduling. Paper [2] derives an entropy regularization formulation for constrained OT problems and introduces a Sinkhorn-type algorithm for equality/inequality constraints, which matches the entropic regularization primitive. Paper [3] proposes a Sinkhorn-Newton method for entropic OT, using logarithmic Newton iterations and validating quadratic convergence, which aligns with the sparse Newton iteration primitive. Paper [26] also provides an entropic regularization approach for multidimensional MOT and uses Newton's method, further confirming mechanism coverage.

### Evaluation
The contribution evaluates using three numerical experiments (option pricing, random cost, diversity-constrained random ranking) with metrics based on \(l_1\) distance to a reference entropy-optimal solution, demonstrating rapid convergence to machine precision. Paper [2] evaluates constrained OT problems using numerical experiments, including random cost setups, and measures convergence to entropy-optimal solutions, which matches the evaluation design. Paper [26] evaluates multidimensional MOT using numerical experiments and convergence metrics, further confirming evaluation coverage.

### Domain
The contribution operates in the domain of optimal transport and numerical optimization, specifically martingale optimal transport. Papers [10], [12], and [26] all address martingale optimal transport problems, making the domain covered.

## Purpose

The contribution's purpose is to solve MOT (martingale optimal transport) problems with (super-)martingale structural constraints efficiently, where each source point has O(n) equality/inequality constraints making standard OT methods inadequate.

Paper [2] explicitly addresses "a general class of OT problems under a combination of equality and inequality constraints" and derives entropy regularization formulations for constrained OT — this is substantively equivalent at the problem-class level. Paper [26] studies "multidimensional martingale optimal transport" with entropic regularization. Paper [12] establishes "numerical methods for solving the martingale optimal transport problem." However, the specific focus on (super-)martingale constraints creating O(n) constraints per source point and the efficiency challenge this poses is most directly addressed by [2] (constrained OT with equality/inequality constraints) and [26] (entropic approximation for MOT). Paper [2] covers the constrained OT purpose; paper [26] covers the MOT-specific purpose.

## Mechanism

The mechanism combines: (1) entropic regularization for MOT, (2) Sinkhorn-type algorithm for constrained OT, (3) sparse Newton iterations exploiting Hessian sparsity (SNS), (4) warm initialization, and (5) geometric η scheduling.

Paper [1] introduces "Sinkhorn algorithm with Sparse Newton Iterations" — explicitly the SNS algorithm exploiting sparsity of the dual Hessian, with warm initialization and annealing schedules. Paper [2] introduces "a Sinkhorn-type algorithm for constrained OT" with entropic regularization for equality/inequality constraints. Paper [26] provides "a new algorithm based on entropic regularization and Newton's method" for martingale OT. Paper [3] proposes "a logarithmic Newton iteration" for entropic OT. The combination of SNS with warm initialization and geometric scheduling applied to MOT is essentially the application of [1]'s mechanism to the MOT setting of [2]/[26].

## Evaluation

The evaluation uses numerical experiments on option pricing benchmarks, comparing against APDAGD baseline, measuring l1 distance to reference entropic solution, with convergence-to-machine-precision as the criterion.

Paper [1] uses numerical experiments comparing Sinkhorn-Newton sparse iterations against baselines (including APDAGD) measuring convergence speed and accuracy. Paper [2] uses numerical experiments on constrained OT problems. Paper [26] uses "numerical experiments" to validate the MOT entropic algorithm. The evaluation design (numerical convergence experiments, comparison to APDAGD baseline, machine precision convergence) matches [1] and [2] closely. Option pricing as a test case appears in [12], [21], [24].

The domain is optimal transport / numerical optimization, specifically martingale optimal transport.

Papers [10], [12], [13], [24], [26] all work in martingale optimal transport. Papers [1], [2], [3], [5], [7], [8] work in optimal transport / numerical optimization. This domain is clearly covered.

Thus, the evaluation is covered.
